resources.string: Add a contact by nickname and exchange keys in person to start a secure conversation.
Your contacts will appear here. No phone number is required — just a nickname and a key fingerprint.
Security profiles, privacy, network and Tor, storage. The default profile is “Paranoid”.
Nickname, avatar, account recovery (mnemonic phrase), multi-device and account transfer.
Multi-layer encryption · Tor by default · No phone number. Your account is a cryptographic key pair, not a number or an e-mail.
Native crypto core not built — account creation unavailable. Build the Rust module (see README.md).
Letters and digits, no phone or e-mail
Protects the mnemonic on this device (Argon2id)
Login: letters, digits and underscore only, no spaces
Login must not be an e-mail address
Login must not be a phone number
Optional. Letters and digits, no phone or e-mail. You can set it later in Settings
A sign-in password is already set
Could not save login and password. Unlock again and retry
Enter your mnemonic phrase (12–24 words separated by spaces). Then set a new password for this device.
Invalid phrase. Check the words and their order.
This device already holds an account. A new one is created only on a clean device: the current account’s conversations, contacts, keys (PSK) and settings will be permanently deleted.
Without a password the account is protected only by the phone’s screen lock: anyone who knows the phone PIN can open your conversations. You can add a password later in Security settings.
This account’s phrase restores access together with the conversations on this device. Another account’s phrase requires a full wipe of the device — you will be asked to confirm.

The current account’s conversations, contacts, encryption keys (PSK), contact requests and settings will be permanently deleted from this device. Its recovery phrase can bring back only the account itself — conversations and contacts on this device will not return.

This phrase belongs to a different account. Before restoring it, the current account’s conversations, contacts, encryption keys (PSK), contact requests and settings will be permanently deleted from this device.

This is the ONLY way to recover your account. Write the phrase on paper and keep it offline. Losing the phrase and password = permanent loss of access to your account and conversations. That is the price of real E2EE — we cannot recover them for you.
Screenshots are blocked (FLAG_SECURE). Do not photograph with another device and do not store the phrase in the cloud.
I wrote down the phrase and understand the risk
Enter your password to unlock account %1$s.
Forgot your password? Recover your account with the mnemonic phrase.
Biometric sign-in unavailable. Enter your password.
Fingerprint sign-in was turned off: the fingerprints on this phone changed or the app’s protection was upgraded. Sign in with your password and turn it on again in Security settings.
Wrong password. Attempts left before the data is wiped: %1$d
Too many wrong attempts. Try again in %1$s
Incoming call. Sign in to see who is calling and answer.
Keys and the sealed record will be destroyed. This is irreversible: without a saved phrase, recovery is impossible.
No phone number — just a nickname and a key fingerprint. Here you exchange the container key (PSK) for layer A manually.
A PSK is a layer-A secret. It is exchanged STRICTLY in person and offline (QR / phrase / NFC) and NEVER travels the network. The server only ever sees the encrypted container.
No container keys yet. Exchange a PSK with your contact in person.
Native crypto core not built — PSK exchange unavailable. Build the Rust module (see README.md).
How to display this contact on your device
Show ONLY in person. The key must not end up in a photo, the cloud or the network. It is never copied to the clipboard.
Screenshots are blocked (FLAG_SECURE). The QR hides automatically after %1$d s.
QR hidden for safety. Tap to show again.
Could not build the QR code. Share the key over NFC or as a mnemonic phrase.
The QR carries the container key (layer A). For an instant secure session (layer B), transfer the full prekey bundle over NFC — hold the devices close while this screen is open.
Or hold the contact’s device close to transfer the key over NFC (while this screen is open).
NFC is unavailable or disabled on this device. Use QR or the phrase.
Point the camera at the contact’s QR (in person only)
Mnemonic phrase (24 words separated by spaces)
Waiting for a tap… Hold the contact’s device where the key is being shown.
Layer A for this contact will stop working until you exchange keys again.
Onion relay address is not set. QR exchange will create the chat and keys, but messages will not be delivered until you enter the relay under Settings → Network and Tor.

The no-Tor server is not configured. QR exchange will create the chat and keys, but messages will not be delivered until you turn Tor on or enter the relay HTTPS address under Settings → Network and Tor.
Onion relay address is not set — messages are not delivered. Enter it in Settings → Network and Tor.
The no-Tor server is not configured — messages are not delivered. Turn Tor on or enter the relay HTTPS address in Settings → Network and Tor.
Debug build — not for real conversations. Developer mode lets anyone extract the data of an open account from it.
AEGIS: container key (PSK) exchange over NFC
Receiving messages over Tor is active
Receiving messages is active (no Tor, direct connection)
New messages. Sign in to read them
Incoming call. Sign in to answer
Hardened with a manual PSK (§6.2) — server MITM ruled out
No manual PSK — verify the code by voice
Media over Tor: more privacy, possible latency
No Tor / direct connection: IP visible to the peer and the server
Networks allow no direct path — media goes through the server\'s relay
Unlock the phone to see who is calling and the verification code.
Native WebRTC is unavailable in this build. Signaling and keys work, but there is no real media stream — the call will not be shown as connected.
The system denied microphone access for the call. Open the app and try again.
The Tor relay is unavailable. The anonymous call was not started so that your IP address stays hidden.
Could not connect: the network blocks the media stream
unavailable — an anonymous call cannot start without it
over Tor — the only media path
server TURN — fallback when there is no direct path
server STUN only: without TURN a peer behind NAT or in Tor mode is unreachable
the server gave no STUN/TURN — only a same-network connection is possible
no manual PSK — verify the code by voice
Could not enable media frame encryption
Frame layer: AES-128-GCM on Signal+PSK keys over DTLS-SRTP
Frame layer not attached — media is DTLS-SRTP only
the network blocks the media stream

Turn recording ON BEFORE the failing action (key exchange, send, call, unlock). The log records detailed app steps, native WebRTC lines, and unclean process death. It contains no secrets (PSK, message text, mailbox ids) — send the file to see which step failed.
Writes a detailed log: account, Tor, relay, key exchange, messages, calls, ICE/TURN, native WebRTC, device sync.
Log is empty — enable recording and retry the action
Built-in Tor (Arti) is not compiled into this build. The indicator does NOT show “connected”: there is no onion traffic and no SOCKS port. Use a full build with the tor feature.
The network mode does not change during a call — switch it after hanging up.
All traffic through the built-in Tor (recommended)
Off: direct HTTPS connection to the AEGIS server
PT binaries are not bundled in this build — only “vanilla” bridges are available.
Built-in Snowflake (disguised as a video call)
Bridge lines (obfs4/snowflake/meek_lite), one per line. The PT binary is substituted automatically from the bundled ones. Fresh bridges — at bridges.torproject.org.
Built-in bridges rotate periodically. If it will not connect — choose “Custom bridges” and paste fresh ones from bridges.torproject.org.
<address>.onion[:port] — a full URL is also accepted
Addresses are discovered automatically (built-in defaults + signed server config). No manual entry needed.
Addresses set manually — automatic updates are not applied. Onion and HTTPS must lead to the same server.
The onion address is tested over Tor. The HTTPS address can only be tested without Tor: a direct connection would reveal your IP.
The HTTPS address is tested directly. The onion address can only be tested with Tor on.
The onion relay address is not set — with Tor, messages are not delivered.
The onion relay address is invalid: a v3 (56-character) .onion is required.
Tor is still connecting — messages will go out once it is up.
The no-Tor server is not configured: the relay HTTPS address is not set. Turn Tor on or enter the address below.
The relay HTTPS address is invalid: https://domain[:port] is required.
Obscures the timing and the fact of sending during delivery (fan-out). Does not affect E2EE of message content — only transport metadata. By default both options follow the security profile.
Randomizes the order and adds delays to drops so a relay observer cannot correlate them by timing. More jitter means more privacy but noticeable delay (including call setup).

Background dummy drops plus padding of real batches with decoys to hide the fact and volume of sending. Active when the relay is reachable (over Tor or HTTPS) and the account is unlocked; uses a little extra traffic/battery.

Login is the public nickname used during key exchange. The password (Argon2id) protects the mnemonic and, through it, the conversation database and PSK keys on this device; it also unlocks biometrics and the duress password.
After saving, this device will require the password to unlock. The mnemonic does not change — keep it stored separately.
The nickname the other person will see at the next key exchange. Cryptographic identity does not change.
Remember the password. Without it and without the mnemonic, access on this device will be lost.
Login and password saved. Biometrics and duress password are now available.

Unlock with fingerprint/face without typing a password. The wrapping key is stored in hardware Keystore/StrongBox and opens only with strong biometrics, not the phone PIN. If a new fingerprint is added in the system, this sign-in turns off and has to be enabled again.
Unavailable for an auto account without a password.
No strong biometrics are configured on this device.
Confirm to bind unlocking to your biometrics
After how many minutes of inactivity (no touches) OR time in the background the app locks automatically: the secret is wiped from memory and a new sign-in is required. Data is not deleted.
Auto-lock is off — the app locks only manually or via the duress password.
A second sign-in password: entering it INSTANTLY destroys the keys (crypto-shredding) instead of unlocking, and the app looks freshly installed. Configurable only for a password-protected account.
After the fifth wrong attempt in a row, sign-in slows down: from 30 seconds up to an hour. With this setting, the tenth failure in a row destroys the data, like the duress password.

An account without a password is protected only by the phone’s screen lock: anyone who knows the phone PIN can open your conversations. Set a password — then the conversation database and PSK keys on this device open only after it is entered.
Failed: at least 8 characters and it must differ from the main one.
Enter a password that will trigger a silent wipe instead of signing in. It must differ from your main password.
Stage 1 — crypto-shredding (instant, irreversible). Stage 2 — best-effort overwrite of free space (≤90%%). On flash storage physical erasure is NOT guaranteed — the main guarantee is stage 1.
All keys, the account, PSKs and the encrypted database will be destroyed. This is irreversible: without a saved phrase, recovery is impossible.
Also overwrite free space (stage 2, slower; no guarantees on flash storage)
No push or FCM: incoming messages arrive via long-poll — over Tor or, without Tor, over HTTPS — and the notification is composed on the device. The server and Google do not know about it (§7.6).
The system has blocked notifications for AEGIS.
Master switch: show notifications about new messages and incoming calls.
Reveal the contact name in the preview. Hidden by default for lock-screen privacy (§14.3).
Reveal the message content in the preview. Hidden by default — “New message” is shown.
Play a sound for a new message.
Play a ringtone for an incoming call.
Synthesized ringtone in the app style instead of the system one. A contact\'s personal ringtone always takes priority.
Ringback for outgoing calls plus negotiation, connect, link-loss and hang-up cues. Played on the voice-call route (earpiece) at call volume.
Show notifications while the app is open (but the chat is not on screen). Turn off to avoid distractions.
Messages older than the chosen period are deleted automatically — both locally and on the server. The %1$d-day cap is hard: it cannot be raised or turned off (§7.3). You can choose a shorter period.
Now: %1$s. This is the maximum allowed period.
Automatically download incoming photos/videos no larger than %1$d MB. Over Tor this is slow; when off, attachments download only on tap (§14.4). Files are always downloaded manually.
Show your contact a double check mark when you read their message. Reciprocal: turning it off hides others’ marks from you too.
Show your contact that you are typing a message.
Reveal “online” / “last seen” to a contact who has the chat with you open.
Blocked contacts: incoming messages are dropped, outgoing ones are not sent (invisibly to the contact).
E2EE over WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP); keys via a Signal session, hardened with a manual PSK (§7.5).
Call media goes over Tor: your IP is hidden from both the server and the peer.
Tor is off: call media goes direct and the peer sees your IP. Encryption is the same.
Warning: native WebRTC is not built in this build — signaling and call-key agreement work, but there is no real media stream.
Call metadata is minimized (§10.10); signaling takes the same path as messages.

AEGIS uses no push services: messages and calls arrive over a persistent connection to the relay (over Tor or direct). The system has to allow the app to work that way — otherwise some calls and messages will not arrive.
Full-screen incoming call is blocked by the system
While it is blocked, a call rings and vibrates but no window with an Answer button appears — the only way to answer is from the notification shade.
Background work is limited by battery optimization

The system freezes the app once it is minimized: an incoming call will not ring or vibrate until you open AEGIS yourself, and messages arrive late. Tap the button below and choose “Allow” in the system dialog.
Background work is blocked: battery mode “Restricted”
In this mode the system stops delivery as soon as the app leaves the screen — calls and messages do not arrive at all. On the app screen that opens, go to “Battery” and choose “Unrestricted”.
Calls will not ring while the app is minimized

AEGIS uses no push services: calls and messages arrive over a persistent connection to the relay. Right now the system limits the app in the background and freezes it soon after you minimize it — an incoming call will not ring or vibrate until you open AEGIS yourself.\n\nAllow AEGIS to run in the background without restrictions: tap “Allow” in the system dialog (or choose “Battery → Unrestricted” on the app screen). You can also do it later under “Settings → Background delivery”.
Calls will not be shown full screen

Since Android 14 the system only lets apps you approved yourself raise a full-screen incoming call. Without that permission a call will ring and vibrate, but no window with an Answer button will appear — you will have to answer from the notification shade.\n\nOpen settings and allow AEGIS full-screen notifications. You can also do it later under “Settings → Background delivery”.

Without notifications you will not learn about an incoming call while the app is minimized: it will not show up on the lock screen or in the shade, and messages will arrive unnoticed. Allow AEGIS notifications — names and text stay hidden on the lock screen.\n\nYou can also do it later under “Settings → Notifications”.
Calls while the account is locked

The account locks itself after inactivity, when you lock it, and after the phone or the app restarts. While it is locked, delivery is currently stopped: calls and messages do not arrive until you sign in again.\n\nTurn on delivery while locked — then a call rings during that time too, only without the caller’s name, and you can answer right after signing in. Your chats stay locked: incoming messages wait in the queue encrypted until you sign in, and the database key is not in memory. You can change this under “Settings → Security”.
Receive while the account is locked
Messages and calls keep arriving while the account is locked and are decrypted after you sign in
Off: while the account is locked, delivery stops — messages and calls do not arrive until you sign in again.

On: the relay connection stays up, and incoming items are queued encrypted and decrypted after you sign in — the database key is not kept in memory. Notifications show neither sender nor text. To answer a call, tap “Answer” and sign in — the call is picked up automatically. If the caller hangs up first, the phone may keep ringing for up to 75 seconds.
The base is dark (§13). “System” follows the device night mode.
Changing the language will restart the screen.

A disguise changes the launcher shortcut and name to a generic utility (§14.1). Notifications also hide the AEGIS name. The system will refresh the shortcut for a moment — that is normal. If the icon does not change, wait a few seconds or restart the launcher.
Shortcut updated. If the home screen still shows the old icon, wait a moment or restart the launcher.
Could not change the icon. Reinstall the app and try again.
Leave empty to restore the original name: %1$s
Leave empty to restore the contact identifier.
All messages in this chat will be deleted on this device only. The contact and keys are kept.
The chat, all messages and the exchange key (PSK) will be removed from this device. Your contact is not affected. You will need a new key exchange to chat again.
No messages yet. The first message will establish a secure session.
“Delete for everyone” (§7.3) asks your contact to delete this message on their side (best-effort, via a secure channel). “Delete for me” affects only this device.
This message was encrypted with the following layers — recorded after a real encrypt/decrypt, not a static claim:
No encryption record for this message: it was stored before this feature existed, or it has not gone through the pipeline yet. New messages show the algorithms that were actually applied.
Layer A not applied (no PSK) — layer B only
Attachment: separate AEAD cascade on a random 256-bit key
Stored on device in SQLCipher (AES-256), never as plaintext files
The contact’s fingerprint is not verified. Tap to compare the safety number (§14.3).
The contact has a new device. Tap to compare the fingerprint (§8).
Layer B keys not received yet — messages will not be sent. The exchange completes on its own once both sides are online (§6.2).
Hold the button · swipe up to lock
Too short: hold the microphone button
Microphone unavailable: check the permission and whether another app is using it
Notifications from this contact are on.
Build a password-encrypted package and hand it to the new device via QR code or file. Neither the package nor the password ever go over the network (§7.1.2).
Multi-device is disabled for this account (§7.1.1). A transfer usually means switching devices. If you want to use two devices at once, enable multi-device in your profile.
Mnemonic and login — required to sign in on the new device
Significantly increases size (file only, not QR)
Without them chats with contacts are unavailable
Scan this QR on the new device. The screen is protected from screenshots (§14.3) — show it in person only.
The package is too large for a QR code (%1$d KB). Save it to a file and move it to the new device (e.g. via offline media).
Receive the transfer package created on the old device and enter the password you set there. The package is transferred offline (§7.1.2).
The package has no account identity — it cannot be applied to a clean device. Build a package with the “Account” item enabled.
Package received. Enter the transfer password.
Crypto core is unavailable in this build.
Transfer password must be at least %1$d characters.
Account is locked — sign in first.
Could not build the transfer package
This is not an AEGIS transfer package.
Unknown format (an AEGIS package was expected).
This device already has an account. Delete it first (§7.4).
The package has no account identity — transfer to a clean device is not possible.
Invalid mnemonic in the transfer package.
Could not derive identity from the mnemonic.
Could not unpack the transfer data
There is no account on this device yet — use import onto a clean device.

Add contacts, conversations and keys (PSK) from a transfer package into the account that ALREADY exists on this device. Merge only adds new items: local data is never overwritten. Identity and Signal state are not transferred.
The package belongs to this same account.
Warning: the package is from a DIFFERENT account. Identity and Signal state are not transferred; chats must be re-established (PSK and a session are required).
Apply settings from the package (overwrites local)
Nothing new to add — everything is already present locally.

Create a password-encrypted package to link a NEW device to this account. It contains the mnemonic, contacts\' public data and Layer A keys, but NOT the Signal state — the new device sets up its own sessions. Transfer the package strictly offline (in person, QR/file).
Multi-device is disabled for this account. Enable it in the profile to link devices.
Scan the QR on the new device in the \"Accept device\" screen, or transfer the file. Share the password over a separate channel.
Show the QR in person. The screen is protected from screenshots.
Accept the linking package from the primary device (QR/file) and enter the linking password. This device becomes part of the account; message history syncs via self-sync.
Multi-device is disabled for this account (§7.1.1). Enable it in the profile.
Device id limit reached (255). Revoke unused devices.
The linking package contains an invalid device id.
Devices on this account. Rename them for convenience or revoke a linked device to stop delivery to it.
Multi-device is disabled for this account. While it is off, a second device will not work; revoking is still available.
No linked devices. Link a device from your profile to use the account on more than one device.
The device will stop receiving new messages and sync; contacts will drop it from delivery. Messages it already received stay on it (§10). This action cannot be undone.

Compare this code with your contact in person or over a trusted channel (e.g. during a call with an already-verified SAS). If the codes match, mark the contact as verified. A match rules out key substitution by an untrusted server (§6.2/§10.7): the code cannot be reproduced without your manual PSK.
The fingerprint was verified offline. The “verified” indicator is shown in the chat.
It is recommended to verify the fingerprint before exchanging sensitive messages (§14.3).
Layer B (Signal) is unavailable in this build — the verification code cannot be computed.
No public key for the contact. Exchange keys in person (§6.2).
No PSK is set for this contact. Exchange a key in person first (§6.2).
Could not compute the verification code.
This contact has multiple devices (multi-device). Each has its own fingerprint — verify each code separately.
No contacts yet. Add a contact via manual key exchange (§6.2).
Invalid recovery phrase (check the words and their order).
Could not obtain the unwrapping key.
Biometric sign-in is not set up.
The account is open: lock it before creating or restoring another one.
This is not an AEGIS exchange code.
Unknown code format (an AEGIS key was expected).
Invalid phrase. Check the words and their order.
Show your own QR first, then scan the contact’s code.
The contact’s code has no account id. Update AEGIS on their device and repeat the exchange.
Could not prepare the key exchange.

The exchange is mutual. Both keep THIS screen open: scan the contact’s QR and let them scan yours. Don’t leave the screen until both show a “✓”. Then compare the safety code in the chat — it must match on both phones.
Your side is ready. Do NOT leave this screen until the contact has scanned your QR, otherwise their exchange won’t complete.
The device does not support ISO-DEP.
The other device is not showing an AEGIS key.
Invalid onion address. Need a v3 (56 characters).onion — a full URL is fine, the https:// scheme is stripped.
Built-in Tor is unavailable in this build
Tor is not running or unavailable
Tor is still connecting. Wait until the status is “connected” and try again.
Success: the relay is reachable via Tor
The relay is unreachable over Tor. Check that the server is running, the address is a .onion (not an https website), and the Tor indicator shows “connected”.
Timed out connecting to the relay over Tor
The onion relay is tested over Tor, and Tor is off.
HTTPS testing is only available without Tor: with Tor on, a direct connection would reveal your IP.
Invalid address: https://domain[:port] without a path is required. http:// is not accepted.
The network mode is switching — try again in a couple of seconds.
Success: the AEGIS relay answers over HTTPS
Something other than an AEGIS relay answers at this address. Check the domain.
The relay answered with HTTP error %1$d
TLS failed: the certificate did not verify (chain, server name or SPKI pin).
HTTPS connection to the relay timed out
The relay is unreachable over HTTPS. Check the network and the address.
Who you are (optional, shown to them)
The strictest option: the layer-A secret is carried physically, never over the network.

Remote add: keys are checked against the address you were given. Not even a compromised server can substitute them — but nothing proves the address itself is authentic, so verify the fingerprint after activation.
Rotating invalidates every address you handed out before. Existing contacts are unaffected.
A public nickname is enumerable: anyone who guesses it learns your accountId and can send you a request. Keys, devices and messages stay private.
Address not recognised. Check that you copied all of it.
User not found. The address may be stale, or the owner has not been online for a long time.
Remote add is unavailable: disabled in settings or not enabled on the relay.
VERIFICATION FAILED (%1$s). The keys do not match the address — substitution is possible. Request NOT sent.
A request to this user is already pending.
Check the accountId and fingerprint over an independent channel before accepting: they are what makes you sure this is the right person.
No contact matches the query. Search covers the chat name, public nickname, accountId and fingerprint — you can paste them straight from the verification screen.
These values are the peer\'s identity. Verify them over an independent channel: the chat name is local and proves nothing.

Permanently deleted from this device: the conversation with %1$s, attachments, the exchange key (PSK), the peer\'s devices and their requests. The peer will not be notified and keeps everything on their side. Re-adding will require a fresh key exchange.

By address: the layer-A secret is never sent over the network — it is derived from a signed handshake, and the server cannot substitute keys. A public nickname additionally makes you findable by name, and enumerable.
The sender learns the request was declined and stops retrying. Turning it off is slightly stricter on metadata.
